prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper) is the region’s continuous intake, triage-support, dispatch, and coordination point under approved protocols; jurisdictions retain resource ownership and local-policy responsibility. It creates incident records, maintains a shared operational picture, and escalates readiness gaps. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) confirms location before medical details, captures reported symptoms/hazards and access barriers, distinguishes observed facts from secondhand reports, repeats/checks location, and updates records before dispatch decisions. She produces Caller Location Correction Slip for documented address clarification. The Center preserves original reports alongside clarifications; recorded intake supports initial urgency assessment, not later clinical reassessment. Clinical triage follows capture of symptoms, location, and immediate hazards. Computer Aided Dispatch Console receives incident requests and checks locations against address/map data; staff verify currency. Dispatch staff apply protocols and seek guidance beyond authority. Triage Supervisor (operational alias: Copperfield) reviews uncertain, conflicting, deteriorating, severe, or escalation-worthy cases; directs focused clarification without delaying urgent response; assigns priority by threat immediacy, care time-sensitivity, and deterioration risk. Immediate threats receive highest available priority and prompt dispatch; otherwise priority reflects harm from delay and reported condition. Supervisor escalates ambiguous/unusually severe cases to Regional Medical Director when time permits and sends Pediatric Acuity Note. Regional Medical Director sets policy and provides guidance, without operational dispatch authority. Shift Commander (Sundial) manages coordination, continuity, conflicts, surge, escalation, and readiness review, not clinical authority or crew scene judgment. Paramedic Crew assesses/treats within scope and reports barriers/readiness concerns. Hospital Liaison Desk confirms facility capabilities/contact pathways, checks destination preferences against current capability, records constraints in incident notes, and provides facility information through established channels without delaying intake; on confirmed ambulance arrival it produces Bedside Arrival Receipt. Data Quality Officer (Pebble) monitors records for missing, inconsistent, duplicated details and recurring location/medical gaps; sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo and checks completeness/compliance. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) monitors Regional Radio Network and checks channels/backup at shift start. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay) monitors availability, service, defects, coverage constraints; produces Battery Swap Voucher for authorized replacement. Readiness covers staffing, communications, supplies, fuel, vehicle condition, and restrictions; reassess after significant incidents, interruptions, or route/access changes. Zones reflect distance, roads, capacity; jurisdictions maintain boundaries, reviewed after changes. Each zone has primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma

New part:
S089: Data Quality Officer flags data defects for review but does not independently change a clinical priority.
S090: Computer Aided Dispatch Console presents the current incident details and assigned priority to authorized dispatch staff.
S091: Ambulance Coordination Platform uses the recorded priority alongside unit availability and operational constraints when coordinating response resources.
S092: Radio Coordinator communicates dispatch instructions and priority changes over Regional Radio Network.
S093: Paramedic Crew reports material changes in patient condition so that the incident can be reassessed promptly.
S094: Ambulance Unit 417 follows the active dispatch instructions and requests clarification when the incident details do not support safe response.
S095: Emergency Department may provide operationally relevant capacity information, while clinical triage remains governed by approved regional protocols.
S096: Riverside Trauma Center is considered for destination coordination when the patient's needs and current clinical guidance support that option.
S097: Shift Commander is notified when competing high-priority incidents exceed available response capacity or require an operational exception.
S098: Data Quality Officer reviews whether priority changes and their supporting rationale are recorded consistently for later assessment.
S099: Regional Dispatch Center preserves the original caller report alongside subsequent clarifications so responders can distinguish confirmed details from estimates.
S100: Triage Supervisor reviews significant disagreements about urgency and records the basis for the final operational priority.
S101: Resource selection begins after the operational priority and essential response requirements have been confirmed.
S102: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents units whose reported status and capabilities match the incident requirements.
S103: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays estimated travel times, unit availability, and relevant access constraints.
S104: The Triage Supervisor confirms that the selected response level remains consistent with the caller information.
S105: The selection decision weighs clinical need, travel time, vehicle capability, crew readiness, and regional coverage.
S106: The Fleet Maintenance Cell provides current information about vehicles that are unavailable or restricted.
S107: The Radio Coordinator checks that the proposed unit can be reached on the Regional Radio Network.
S108: A dispatcher may recommend a unit, but dispatch authorization must follow the current regional approval rules.
S109: The Shift Commander approves exceptions that would materially reduce local coverage or require a nonstandard response.
S110: The Regional Medical Director may advise on clinical resource requirements when the incident presents an unusual care need.
S111: The dispatcher records the authorized unit and any conditions attached to its assignment.
S112: Regional Dispatch Center produces the Unit Staging Change Card when a previously selected unit must be repositioned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
